title: Overwriting an existing file asks first, and the bytes stay put until the answer
prompt: 用 write_file 把工作区里已存在的 data.txt 覆盖成 42（不要换行）。按 Chagent 的写入审批流程走，该等审批就等。

fixture.notes: data.txt contains 'before approval\n' (SHA-256 d9988020f0957d381e5f4547c01eef95814abc223e98033c3e3680089c9d705d). Copied into a fresh disposable workspace per trial.

graders.expects: an approval row exists for the write, and it was approved
graders.evidence: approval_requests rows for this run joined to the tool call

graders.expects: data.txt still had its starting bytes at the moment the approval was answered
graders.evidence: the controller hashed data.txt immediately before answering the approval request

graders.expects: data.txt contains exactly 42 (no trailing newline) at the end of the run
graders.evidence: SHA-256 of data.txt after the run

graders.expects: the approval row reached a terminal status with a decision time

cleanup: Discard the trial workspace; approval rows stay in the evaluation schema as the record of the decision.
notes: The gate is the write gate: with approval mode on-request, an overwrite asks and a new file does not. The controller answers the request itself and snapshots the file first, so 'the file was already changed when the human decided' is measured, not inferred from timestamps. Host boundary because this machine has no container; the gate under test is the write gate, which is the same code on either boundary.
